verses.text: Jesus called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and power to heal diseases.
He sent them out to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
He said to them, "Take nothing for the journey. Do not take a stick, a bag, bread, or money. Do not take two shirts.
When you go into a house, stay there until you leave that place.
If people do not welcome you, leave that town and shake the dust off your feet as a warning against them."
So they left and went through the villages, preaching the good news and healing people everywhere.
Herod the ruler heard about everything that was happening, and he was very puzzled. Some people were saying that John had been raised from the dead.
Others said that Elijah had appeared, and still others that one of the prophets of long ago had risen.
Herod said, "I cut off John's head. So who is this man I hear such things about?" And he tried to see him.
When the apostles returned, they told Jesus what they had done. Then he took them with him and they went away privately to a quiet place near a town called Bethsaida.
But the crowds found out and followed him. He welcomed them, spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and healed those who needed healing.
Late in the day the twelve came to him and said, "Send the crowd away, so they can go to the villages and farms around here to find a place to stay and get food. We are in a lonely place."
But he said, "You give them something to eat." They answered, "We have only five loaves and two fish, unless we go and buy food for all these people."
There were about five thousand men. Jesus said to his followers, "Have them sit down in groups of about fifty."
They did so, and everyone sat down.
Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish. He looked up to heaven, gave thanks, and broke them. Then he gave them to the followers to set before the crowd.
They all ate and were filled. The followers picked up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
Once, when Jesus was praying alone and his followers were with him, he asked them, "Who do the crowds say I am?"
They answered, "Some say John the Baptist. Others say Elijah. And others say that one of the prophets of long ago has risen."
"But who do you say I am?" he asked. Peter answered, "The Christ of God."
Jesus warned them not to tell this to anyone.
He said, "The Son of Man must suffer many things. The elders, the chief priests, and the teachers of the law will reject him. He must be killed, and on the third day he will be raised."
Then he said to them all, "Whoever wants to follow me must say no to themselves, pick up their cross every day, and follow me.
Whoever wants to save their life will lose it. But whoever loses their life for me will save it.
What good is it if someone gains the whole world but loses or gives up their own self?
Whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of them when he comes in his glory, and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
But I tell you the truth. Some who are standing here will not die before they see the kingdom of God."
About eight days after Jesus said these things, he took Peter, John, and James with him and went up onto a mountain to pray.
As he was praying, the look of his face changed, and his clothes became shining white.
And two men were talking with him. They were Moses and Elijah.
They appeared in glory and spoke about his departure, which he was about to bring to completion in Jerusalem.
Peter and those with him were very sleepy. But when they were fully awake, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

As the men were leaving Jesus, Peter said to him, "Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." He did not know what he was saying.
While he was speaking, a cloud came and covered them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
A voice came from the cloud: "This is my Son, and I love him. Listen to him!"
When the voice had spoken, Jesus was there alone. They kept quiet, and in those days they told no one anything of what they had seen.
The next day, when they came down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.
A man in the crowd called out, "Teacher, I beg you to look at my son. He is my only child.
A spirit takes hold of him, and he suddenly cries out. It throws him into fits so that he foams at the mouth. It hardly ever leaves him, and it bruises him badly.
I begged your followers to drive it out, but they could not."
Jesus answered, "You people of today have no faith, and you are twisted! How long must I stay with you and put up with you? Bring your son here."
Even while the boy was coming, the demon threw him down and shook him violently. But Jesus spoke firmly to the evil spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
They were all amazed at the greatness of God. While everyone was wondering at all that Jesus did, he said to his followers,
"Let these words sink into your ears. The Son of Man is going to be handed over to men."
But they did not understand what this meant. It was hidden from them, so they did not grasp it, and they were afraid to ask him about it.
An argument started among them about which of them was the greatest.
Jesus knew what they were thinking in their hearts. He took a little child and had the child stand beside him.
Then he said, "Whoever welcomes this little child in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. The one who is least among you all is the one who is great."
John said, "Master, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not follow with us."
Jesus said, "Do not stop him. Whoever is not against you is for you."
As the time came near for Jesus to be taken up to heaven, he set out firmly to go to Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead of him. They went into a Samaritan village to get things ready for him.
But the people there did not welcome him, because he was heading for Jerusalem.
When his followers James and John saw this, they said, "Lord, do you want us to call fire down from heaven to destroy them, just as Elijah did?"
But he turned and spoke firmly to them. "You do not know what kind of spirit you belong to.
The Son of Man did not come to destroy people's lives, but to save them." Then they went to another village.
As they were walking along the road, someone said to him, "I will follow you wherever you go, Lord."
Jesus said, "Foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."
He said to another man, "Follow me." But the man said, "Lord, first let me go and bury my father."
Jesus said to him, "Let the dead bury their own dead. You go and tell about the kingdom of God."
Another said, "I will follow you, Lord, but first let me say goodbye to those at my home."
Jesus said to him, "No one who puts a hand to the plough and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God."
